name: AI Chat Inbox
tagline: An inbox-style front end for AI chat threads: one place to run, search and organize conversations across models.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This category is a thin, pleasant wrapper around model APIs you already pay for, and wrappers are the easiest thing an agent builds. Threads, tags, archive, full text search and a model switcher are a few hundred lines with SQLite and a streaming chat SDK. There is no network effect here: your value is your own conversation history, which is a local database file. What you will not get in one session is the polish, the mobile experience and the long tail of provider quirks like tool calls, attachments and vision inputs. If you mostly want a tidy home for your own prompts and threads, build it and keep your keys.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a local inbox UI where you start threads against any configured model provider, then tag, archive, search and export the whole history from a SQLite file you own.
requirements: At least one model provider API key (OpenAI, Anthropic or similar)
Willingness to pay per token instead of per month
whatYouLose: A polished mobile app or anything that syncs between your laptop and your phone
Attachments, images, file parsing and tool calling unless you keep building
Someone else absorbing provider API changes and deprecated model names
Hosted backups: your history lives in one file you are now responsible for
moatNotes: The defensible part is UX taste and keeping up with a dozen provider APIs, not data or scale.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a hosted wrapper handles the boring parts: it works on your phone, it survives a model rename, it renders markdown and code well, and it does not ask you to think about your own database. Bundled billing is also genuinely convenient for people who do not want to manage keys and per-token spend. That is real value, it is just value with a short half-life, since every incumbent chat app ships the same features eventually.
notes: Multi-model chat wrappers are the hello world of the AI era, which is both a compliment to the builders and a warning to their pricing page.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user "AI chat inbox" web app. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/inbox.db, migrations run on boot
- Vercel AI SDK for streaming chat, providers: OpenAI and Anthropic
- Runs with: npm install && npm run dev on localhost:3000

Data model:
- threads: id, title, model, provider, created_at, updated_at, archived (bool), pinned (bool)
- messages: id, thread_id, role (user|assistant|system), content (text), model, token_estimate, created_at
- tags: id, name; thread_tags: thread_id, tag_id

UI, three panes like a mail client:
- Left: filters (Inbox, Pinned, Archived, by tag), plus a model picker
- Middle: thread list with title, last message snippet, relative time, tag chips
- Right: the conversation, streaming assistant replies, markdown plus code blocks with copy buttons
- Keyboard: n = new thread, e = archive, / = focus search, cmd+enter = send

Features in scope:
- Streaming responses, stop button, retry last message, edit-and-resend a user message (truncates the thread after it)
- Auto-title a new thread from the first exchange with one cheap model call
- Full text search across messages using SQLite FTS5, highlight matches in the thread list
- Per-thread system prompt, plus a library of reusable saved prompts
- Export: one thread or everything to JSON and to markdown files
- Rough cost display per thread from token estimates, config in a simple prices.ts map

Explicitly out of scope: attachments, images, tool calling, RAG, multi-user, sharing, auth, deployment.

Secrets: read OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env.local, ship .env.example, never log keys. If a key is missing, hide that provider in the picker instead of crashing.

Deliverables: working app, seed script with two example threads, and a README with setup, keyboard shortcuts, and where the database file lives so I can back it up.
